text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Parliament began debate Wednesday of a social insurance package.
- The cabinet is expected today to discuss a bill allowing foreigners to buy farmland.
- All opposition parties are against allowing foreigners to buy farmland.
- Opposition party Christian Democrats will hold national board elections on June 21.

- Presidents Arpad Goncz and Emil Constantinescu have issued a joint statement of gratitude to US President Bill Clinton for his message of congratulations on the occasion of the first meeting of the Hungarian and Romanian heads of state.
- Hungary and Russia signed a protocol agreement Tuesday on cooperation in minority policy.
- Postabank's small shareholders and senior management will meet today, one day before the AGM on Friday.

- The Finance Ministry made public its three-year macroeconomic forecast Wednesday, as approved by the government last week. Under this, GDP is expected to grow 3% this year, 3-4% in 1998 and 1999, and 4-5% in the year 2000.
- Public sector real wages rose 10% in the first quarter compared to the same period of last year.
- Oil storage company Koolajtarolo Rt. is set to construct a new, 480,000 cubic meter storage facility, financed by a $95 million line of credit from Credit Lyonnais, ING Bank and CIB Hungaria Bank.
